label: Blue Note
rationale: The peak studio statement of the Morgan/Shorter/Timmons Jazz Messengers — AllMusic calls it the group hitting its artistic peak, Penguin Guide 4 stars, Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 5 stars, DownBeat 4 stars on release. The 11-minute title track is one of the defining hard-bop performances, and with Moanin' and Free for All already in the canon, this is the missing middle chapter of the Messengers' golden era.

Engineer credit: no source names the engineer; per the Van Gelder inference rule (Blue Note, 1960, confirmed Van Gelder Studio) engineer recorded as Rudy Van Gelder with epistemic inf. CD/reissue bonus tracks 'When Your Lover Has Gone' and 'Sincerely Diana (alternate take)' excluded per contract (reissue-only). Original liner notes by Barbara J. Gardner. Per-track personnel listed as full quintet by inference from the single-ensemble session; no source assigns musicians per track.

ballot.album: Art Blakey & The Jazz Messengers — A Night in Tunisia (1960)
ballot.case_for: This is a peak document by the Morgan/Shorter/Timmons Jazz Messengers, a lineup whose personnel gravity captures hard bop's meeting of Blakey's propulsion, Morgan's virtuosity, Timmons's gospel-rooted rhythmic force, and Shorter's emerging compositional modernism. Its 11-minute recasting of Gillespie and Paparelli's "A Night in Tunisia" is a defining hard-bop performance, while Shorter's "Sincerely Diana" and Morgan's "Yama" and "Kozo's Waltz" document the band developing the book that would lead from Moanin' toward Free for All. The dossier further records strong guide recognition—Penguin Guide four stars, Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide five stars, DownBeat four stars, and AllMusic's artistic-peak assessment—and the Blue Note/Van Gelder setting reinforces its discovery value as a vivid, accessible statement of the tradition.
ballot.case_against: The critical ratings establish esteem but do not, on the supplied evidence, demonstrate repeated placement on independent consensus canon lists; the dossier's substantive support is mainly Wikipedia and AllMusic rather than primary reviews, liner notes, or a discographical source. The album's reputation is disproportionately concentrated in its extended treatment of a Gillespie standard, and the remaining originals, though important evidence of Morgan and Shorter's development, are less widely established as individual touchstones. Its two-session documentation also remains incomplete at track level, with production and personnel detail partly inferred.
ballot.disagreement: One reference regards the combined critical reception, defining title performance, and landmark lineup as sufficient for consensus_core and must_have status; the other finds the consensus evidence thinner than that of unambiguous core entries and judges the album's impact too front-loaded to clear that threshold, favoring contested and strong.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes that John treat this as a high-priority contested hard-bop candidate, with its exceptional title performance and lineup weighed against the less fully demonstrated album-wide consensus.
